lines.en: That was a metaphor, in case you still haven’t picked up on my affinity for those yet.
Today, it isn’t raining at all.
To splash is to exist. And the puddles are air-pockets I don’t belong in as my true home is the ocean.
This amphibious shell makes breathing on land possible, but I know where it is I really belong.
Somewhere far away from here — filled with people I can relate to about things I care about.
But instead, my air-pocket today is the backseat of a car I’ve found myself in before.
The two girls joining me here, while they may look similar to the last one, are not the same.
And I cannot relate to either of them at all, for they were not born with skin as permeable as mine.
They can not survive in the water, and puddles like this are seen as nothing more than things to play in.
So as this external lung unsuccessfully siphons the bad out of the good and takes it all in as one singular dose of half-tainted oxygen, I wish I was born with fur.
That way, I wouldn’t have to deal with any of this.
And I could touch anything I wanted without fear of contamination.
: You look kind of weird, Jeeves. Weirder than normal, I mean- since you look pretty weird in general.
: Tsukasa is right. You seem a tad bit “out of your element” right now. Could it be that Chika’s nostalgic tales have cast a shadow on you the same way they did me?
: Yeah, that has to be it. There’s no way being in the back of a car with two girls from the wealthiest family in all of Kumon-mi would take me “out of my element.” This is clearly where I belong.
: Is commoner sarcasm always so snarky and unfunny? Or are you just bad at making jokes?
: Tsukasa, be nice. We may not be at the manor, but Sensei is still our guest. And we must treat him with the same level of respect we’d treat anyone else.
: Yes, Mother. Can I ask a question, though?
: Of course, dear.
: Why do we have to drive him home when he said he was okay with walking? Isn’t doing that just unnecessarily flaunting how rich we are?
: There is a difference between doing something to flaunt one’s wealth and doing something out of the kindness of one’s heart.
: If you’d like a better explanation, look no further than your older sister as the two of you seem to approach this matter in completely different ways.
: My way is better. People are always taking advantage of Onee-sama because she has a heart. Do you think Jeff Bezos or Elon Musk have hearts, Mother? Because I don’t. And they rule the world.
: Well, until you rule the world, please try and be more like your sister.
: Tsukasa’s right, though.
: I am?
: Not about the wealth thing — though, I will agree you’re not entirely wrong in that regard. But I was talking more about the “driving me home” part.
: You didn’t have to go this far out of your way for me, even if it was out of the kindness of your heart.
: Nonsense. It’s no trouble at all. In fact, I’m glad things worked out this way as it gives me a rare opportunity to capitalize on something I’ve been particularly interested in.
: There’s my mother. I knew you wouldn’t have gone through this much trouble if you didn’t have something to gain from it.
: So, what I’m hearing is that this is less “giving me a ride home” and more “kidnapping me to get something you want.”
: Well, if you’d like to make me sound like some sort of villain, I suppose there would be a bit of truth to that.
: Well, what can I give you that your money can’t?
: Oh, and if it’s something you can’t say in front of Tsukasa for reasons, just wink at me. I will understand.
: Mother, what did that mean? Jeeves is trying to speak cryptically, but isn’t smart enough to do it properly so it didn’t make much sense to me.
: Nothing, Tsukasa. And that is most assuredly not what I have “kidnapped” Sensei for.
: I simply wanted to see the property my oldest daughter invested in. That’s all.
: Joining the world of real estate is a very respectable decision to make at Touka’s age. Even if that decision was only partially made with her future in mind and not someone else’s.
: Well, ignoring the fact that I thought we were on the way to my actual home, it’s not like I pressured Touka into that or anything. I straight up told her I wouldn’t accept it.
: And yet you did accept it. Curious.
: She wouldn’t take no for an answer.
: Touka rarely takes no for an answer. Do you cave to all of these assertions, or just the ones that greatly benefit you?
: Why do you look so threatened? Did I hit the nail on the head?
: Kind of. But if I look threatened, it’s probably more due to the fact that I know you could murder me and cover it up without any trouble at all.
: Nonsense. There would be a little bit of trouble. But I can promise you that you’re in good hands.
: Touka would be quite disappointed if her favorite teacher mysteriously vanished, of course.
: So, what then? You just want to see my apartment and then you’ll release me from your villainous clutches?
: You think you can break free from my grasp that easily?
: No. And I also think I probably look slightly more threatened right now.
: I think you should look slightly more threatened right now. I’m a very powerful woman, Sensei.
: Mother, is this what “flirting” is?
: What? Where did you learn that?
: Jeeves, there are easier ways of getting inside Tsukioka Manor than engaging in an affair with my mother. You don’t have to try that hard. The butler offer is still on the table.
: Tsukasa, that is absolutely not what is going on right now. It was playful bantering. Right, Sensei?
: It kind of felt like flirting near the end there. I won’t lie.
: Ugh, fantastic. Now, Tsukasa’s curiosity is going to be piqued and we’ll need to start her on “those” slideshows even earlier than anticipated. And she was already ahead of schedule.
: Do I have to watch those? Onee-sama didn’t leave her wing of the manor for a full week after she watched them and that makes me kind of worried.
: I will not argue if you also wind up staying in your wing for a week after all is said and done. Or longer.
: You two can look around the apartment. I doubt it will be any fun, though. I haven’t really changed anything yet.
: Oh, Tsukasa won’t be joining us. It will just be you and me.
: What?! Why?! I want to see Onee-sama’s low-income housing too! You know I love low-income housing!
: What I know is that you need to go to sleep or you’ll be grumpy for your classes in the morning.
: I already know everything in those classes! I want to learn more about real estate so I can help you and Onee-sama next year!
: No means no, Tsukasa.
: But Mother-
: No talking back. Responsibility first, leisure second. If you do well tomorrow, then we can return to your sister’s building. Tonight, you will go to sleep.
: ...Fine. But only because I’m extremely mature and goal-oriented.
: This all works for you, correct?
: Does it even matter? You’re just going to talk me into it if I say no.
: See? I told you it was impossible to escape my grasp.
The driver stops by Tsukioka Manor and drops Tsukasa off, who is then promptly escorted inside by an unnecessarily large amount of bodyguards and staff members.
I’m not sure what would have happened within the thirty seconds it took for them to make it down the walkway, but I guess that doesn’t matter as it's now fading from my vision anyway.
When we eventually make it to my apartment, Tsubasa takes it upon herself to start traipsing around as if she owns the place. Which...I guess she kind of does.
But that doesn’t make it any less weird.
In fact, this whole situation is weird.
I get wanting to check out the building her daughter invested in, but that could have been done without me.
There are plenty of other rooms without tenants here. So either there’s more to this than she’s letting on or-
: I assume you’ve caught on by now that this is a little more than a quick walkthrough to inspect the property.
: ...Yeah.
: I should have figured that out when you wouldn’t let Tsukasa come.
: Oh?
: Then, since you appear to have slipped into detective-mode, tell me...what do you think I was trying to gain by coming here alone with you in the middle of the night?
: Well?
: I mean...common sense would probably say sex.
: Is that your final answer?
: It would make the most sense.
: You’re a seemingly...dissatisfied married woman with enough power and money to ensure I wouldn’t talk about it. Which I wouldn’t do anyway, but still.
: And you’re certainly calculating enough to ensure we wouldn’t get caught.
: But?
: But...I feel like that’s not it.
: Then what is?
: Something...with Chika? Or Touka?
: Are you just guessing at this point?
: Kind of, yeah.
: Hmm...
: Do you have any champagne? Or wine?
: I...do not.
: I suppose I’ll have to get you some as a housewarming present, then. It’s bad manners to keep your house-guests thirsty, you know.
: I mean...it’s not like I was expecting-
: It’s bad manners to not offer them a seat as well.
: Would you...like to sit?
: I thought you’d never ask.
Tsubasa steps forward and...takes a seat on the bed?
Is she actually here for sex after all?
: Hmm...the decor is a bit bland for my tastes. But overall, I’d say this is an acceptable staging for Touka’s first property.
: You really lucked out getting this for free, didn’t you?
: Like I said, I wasn’t asking for this.
: How many people know about this place?
: Counting you? About...a handful.
There could have been more, but the world took them away.
: So...three others apart from my daughter and me.
: I see.
: Is your niece one of them?
: She’s not.
: Is Chika one of them?
: She’s...not.
: Interesting.
: May I ask what you intend to use it for? You already have a house of your own. And, from what I understand, it’s your niece who takes care of you, so...
: You’re likely not intending to live here, correct?
: I don’t really have any idea what I’m going to use this place for just yet.
: Are you open to suggestions?
: I...guess?
: Do you have something in mind?
: To begin, I think this would be an acceptable substitution for Touka’s bedroom the next time you engage in violent sex with a teenage girl.
: Yeah...that’s a pretty reasonable suggestion. I’ll keep it in mind.
: Was the barking your idea or hers?
: Are you actually interested or are you just winding up to something?
: Can it not be both?
: I take it that means it’s both.
: I am a woman of questionable morals at times.
: Would I act as you do and go out of my way to engage in illicit relations with high schoolers? No. More than likely, not.
: But would I leave the door cracked and peer through as you do that for several minutes while questioning my sanity? Perhaps.
: Did you enjoy the show?
: I enjoyed that you two enjoyed it. You seemed just as enthralled with one another as the day I first met you.

: Whether it be her body alone, the taboo nature of taking something you’re not allowed to have, or genuine love...I know not. But we’ve already discussed this once before and I don’t mean to do it again.
: Then...what do you intend to-
: Why not share in this newfound convenience with someone who needs it more?
: Why not ask Chika and her sister if they’d like to move in?
: That’s a lot more wholesome of a suggestion than I expected based on your...demeanor ever since we left her apartment.
: If I don’t keep you on your toes, you might wind up getting the better of me someday. And we can’t have that, can we?
: Doesn’t matter. Chika already said no to your hospitality. And sure, you were inviting her to come live in your mansion, but I doubt she would have accepted this either.
: As do I. Her will is far stronger than it should be for a girl her age. And her experience growing up with close to nothing has skewed her perception of just how meaningless material goods are.
: Says the woman with more “material goods” than anyone.
: It’s because I have everything that I know just how little any of it matters.
: I’ll never actually replace her mother. Nor do I intend to. And even if Chika appreciates the role I’ve somehow wound up with in her life, I think she feels a little guilty.
: If I were her and the last connection I had with my mother apart from some jewelry and makeup were the memories of a home...and some other woman tried to whisk me away from that-
: I’d almost surely say no as well.
: But that’s different from a person she’s in love with asking her. You wouldn’t be “replacing” anyone.
: You’d be the next step in her life...or a chance for her to grow without convincing herself she’s abandoned what little she has left.
: But it wouldn’t be the right step.
: Not even if it would make her safe?
: You know very well she’s not safe with me.
: Because you’re having consensual sex with her slightly before you’re supposed to be? That’s silly.
: She’ll be safer because she’ll have stability...and she won’t have to worry about living in an area where people are defecating on the streets.
: I’d never force her to walk away from important memories...that would be insensitive and it is just not the type of person I am.
: The type of person I actually am would subtly convince her that what she wants isn’t what she needs...all while slowly guiding her from the shadows into a safer, healthier life.
: It’s manipulation in the good way. It’s stripping away the things that could potentially hurt her, all while setting her up for success.
: As the new matriarch in her life, it’s my duty to keep an eye on things like that. And, apologies if this dehumanizes you, but you’re a tool I need in order to get that done.
: Kind of like how I was a tool to start moving Touka forward as well?
: Exactly.
: I look out for my girls.
: And we both know she’d be better off if she could free herself from that cage of responsibility she was locked in when her mother died.
: She can’t do it alone...and she won’t accept help from someone who can help her because it will make her feel like she’s failed.
: But she’ll accept it from someone who can’t.
: At this rate, she won’t accept my aid until her sister falls ill. And by then, it may already be too late.
: We can change that if we work together.
: I can handle the financials and the motherly bonding-
: And you can be the curtain maintaining the illusion that she’s doing it all on her own.
: This would be way easier if she’d just accept how shitty her life is.
: I don’t know if she’d have ever made it this far to begin with if she’d done that.
: Sometimes, those less fortunate than us need to refute reality entirely to create a world that feels like it’s worth living in.
: They trick themselves into seeing a light at the end of a tunnel even when everything is dark...and it’s that false chase that keeps them occupied enough to never give up or turn around.
: When you have nothing, you’re forced to create something.
: What happens when you have everything?
: You share it.
: Tell that to Jeff Bezos or Elon Musk.
: The only thing I’d tell them is to shove it.
: Talk to Chika. Convince her that coming here is the right move.
: I can’t just ask her to move in with me, though. If she finds out Touka gave me this place, it’ll open a whole can of worms and spiral into...terrified jealousy or something. I know her.
: Then just tell her you bought it yourself. Or-
: Ah!
: I’m a genius!
: I’m already aware of that. You don’t have to brag about it.
: The key is quite literally making her think she’s done this on her own.
: So if we frame it as a new, affordable apartment complex with a rate that wouldn't immediately dissuade her, she’ll be able to get out of that god-forsaken section of Kumon-mi once and for all.
: Maybe, but that still doesn’t change the fact that she’s got an extreme emotional attachment to her current place.
: But she has an extreme emotional attachment to you as well. That’s what I’ve been trying to explain all along.
: I don’t know, Tsubasa...we can try, but-
: I’m going to call my daughter. The more bearable one. But think more about what I said.
: You said a lot of things tonight, so if you could give me like one major theme or idea to ponder over while you’re gone, that would be nice.
: Hmm...I suppose I can pose a question. Does that work?
: Sure.
: Then...
: What matters more — the livelihood of those you care about...or a life of unparalleled convenience?
: Ooh, and here’s another one — how much work are you willing to put in to help someone resistant to change?
: Oh! And also-
: That’s enough. I’m good with just those two questions. Thanks.
: One more. That’s all.
: Ugh...fine.
: Can you still love someone if they’re always right beside you?
Tsubasa leaves before I can tell her I already have an answer to that last question.
It was just someone else who helped me figure it out.
Tsubasa’s affection has increased to [tsubasa_love]!
